subject: Pilot scope & access roadmap — Asteria Health
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@asteriahealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot scope & access roadmap — Asteria Health

Emma — thanks again for a focused conversation earlier today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps to get the pilot moving.

Pain points you called out:
- Frequent false positives in triage routing (manual review overhead).
- Latency spikes when batch volumes increase (esp. end-of-day).
- No established evaluation suite for prompt drift/safety.

High-level pilot goal:
- Demonstrate that Redwood can reduce manual triage volume by 40% while keeping precision >= 85% on the same dataset, at median p95 latency < 200ms.

Proposed scope (4-week pilot):
1) Week 0 (kickoff): access & baseline — provide a small labeled dataset (5k rows) and a sample streaming endpoint for smoke tests.
2) Week 1: integrate prompt set (we’ll ship 30 representative prompts + edge cases).
3) Week 2: run staged evaluation (quality + latency) and tune batching/quantization profile.
4) Week 3: handover report, operational playbook, and decision checkpoint.

Success metrics (to be agreed):
- Precision >= 85% and recall tradeoff review
- Manual reviews reduced by 40% relative to baseline
- Median latency < 120ms, p95 < 200ms with your typical traffic profile

Immediate asks from Asteria:
- S3 link or secure share of a 500–1,000 record sample + schema
- Network/MFA details for our staging instance (we’ll need CIDR/IP allowlist)
- Security contact to kick off the brief questionnaire

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft mutual action plan (MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx) and our minimal network requirements (network_requirements.pdf).

If this looks right, can we: (a) confirm the two success metrics above, (b) share a shortlist of stakeholders and a feasible date for an internal kickoff (we propose Monday Oct 5), and (c) confirm whether we should proceed on a staging VPC or via a short-lived API key for initial smoke tests?

Thanks — I’ll loop Jordan in to start the environment checklist once we have your confirmation.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Ben — thanks for the concise recap, this matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Metrics: we agree on precision target of 85% as a minimum. For manual-review reduction, let’s target 35% as a stretch (we can update to 40% after we see early runs).
2) Data: I’ll share a redacted sample (CSV) via our secure ShareBox — expect a link tomorrow.
3) Access: staging VPC is preferred due to PHI-related controls; Rajiv (cc’d, our CTO) will own network setup.
4) Stakeholders:
   - Emma Johnson — Product (pilot owner)
   - Rajiv Menon — CTO (network & security approver)
   - Priya Desai — Clinical Ops (will provide labeled examples) — I’ll introduce via calendar if needed.

Procurement note: there is a brief SOW/PO approval step — I will work with procurement but do not expect this to block the kickoff next week.

Kickoff: Oct 5 works for us; please send a calendar invite. Also please confirm whether you need a non-prod account provisioned for our engineers (preferred) or whether we should go via API key for initial smoke tests.

Thanks,
Emma
Senior PM, Asteria Health

Emma / Ben — following up with the technical checklist we’ll use to confirm environment readiness. I’ll coordinate with Rajiv for allowlist and handshake.

Technical kickoff checklist (pre-kickoff items we’ll verify in the first 30 minutes):
- Network: CIDR/IP allowlist or peering details from Asteria (Rajiv) — needed for staging VPC access
- Data: sample CSV received and verified (schema matches) — Emma to confirm S3/ShareBox link
- Auth: confirm whether to use short-lived API keys or mutual TLS / token broker for staging (Asteria prefers VPC + keyless access)
- Logging & Audit: ensure request logs go to your audit bucket (we’ll provide pattern)
- Size & Rate: provide expected qps and max sequence lengths so we can tune batching (Emma — a 1-hour sample traffic profile is ideal)

Deliverables during pilot:
- Prompt set: 30 canonical prompts + 12 edge-case prompts (Monica will author; deliverable due by Oct 8)
- Eval dashboard: automated daily evals (precision/recall & latency histogram) — Monica will share the first snapshot on Oct 12
- Ops playbook: runbook for failover and model rollback — Jordan to deliver before the final checkpoint

Attachments referenced: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx, network_requirements.pdf

Task assignments:
- Rajiv (Asteria): provide CIDR and procurement contact
- Emma: share sample link and Priya’s contact
- Kimberly Park (Redwood): I’ll hand over the SOC2 questionnaire and timeline (Kimberly, please pick this up)
- Monica Patel (Redwood): will prepare the prompt set and daily eval dashboard

Links:
